questions.q: Where does the psalmist say he takes refuge?
questions.a: The psalmist says he takes refuge in Yahweh.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do for him?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to deliver and rescue him, to consider his situation and save him.

questions.q: What does the psalmist want Yahweh to be to him?
questions.a: The psalmist wants Yahweh to be his savior and his protector.

questions.q: From whose hand does the psalmist want to be rescued?
questions.a: He wants to be rescued from the hand of the wicked, and from the one who does wrong and the one who is cruel.

questions.q: How long has the psalmist trusted in Yahweh?
questions.a: He has trusted in Yahweh since he was young.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say that he will do continually?
questions.a: He says that he will always praise Yahweh.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh?
questions.a: He says that Yahweh is his refuge and mighty protector.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask to do all day?
questions.a: He asks to be able to praise Yahweh all day.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask God not to do when the psalmist is old and his strength fails?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh not to cast him away or forsake him.

questions.q: What do the enemies of the psalmist say as they are plotting against him?
questions.a: They say that God is not helping him, that they should pursue and seize him because God will not save him.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do quickly?
questions.a: The psalmist asks God not to be far from him and to hurry to help him.

questions.q: What does the psalmist want to happen to those who are hostile to his life?
questions.a: He wants them to be put to shame and disgraced, and he wants their plans to fail.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say he will continue to do?
questions.a: The psalmist says he will hope and trust continually and will continue to praise Yahweh.

questions.q: What will the psalmist proclaim with his mouth about Yahweh?
questions.a: He will tell of Yahweh’s righteousness and salvation all day.

questions.q: In whose strength does the psalmist say he will come?
questions.a: The psalmist says he will come in the strength of Lord Yahweh.

questions.q: Why should Yahweh not forsake the psalmist?
questions.a: Yahweh should not forsake him because the psalmist is declaring Yahweh’s wonderful doings to the next generation and his power to everyone who is to come.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about God’s righteousness?
questions.a: The psalmist says that God’s righteousness reaches to the heights and that no one is like God.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do after he has experienced many troubles?
questions.a: The psalmist asks God to revive him and to give him a good life again.

questions.q: For what does the psalmist give thanks with his harp?
questions.a: He gives thanks to God for God’s faithfulness.

questions.q: What does the psalmist do all day long?
questions.a: He meditates on God’s righteousness all day long.

commentary.text: Prayers that God would deliver and save.

Verses 1–13 David prays that he might never be made ashamed of dependence upon God. With this petition every true believer may come boldly to the throne of grace. The gracious care of Divine providence in our birth and infancy, should engage us to early piety. He that was our Help from our birth, ought to be our Hope from our youth. Let none expect ease or comfort from the world. Those who love the Lord, often are hated and persecuted; men wondered at for their principles and conduct; but the Lord has been their strong refuge. The faithful servants of God may be assured that he will not cast them off in old age, nor forsake them when their strength fails.

The psalmist declares that the righteousness of Christ, and the great salvation obtained thereby, shall be the chosen subject of his discourse. Not on a sabbath only, but on every day of the week, of the year, of his life. Not merely at stated returns of solemn devotion, but on every occasion, all the day long. Why will he always dwell on this? Because he knew not the numbers thereof. It is impossible to measure the value or the fulness of these blessings. The righteousness is unspeakable, the salvation everlasting. God will not cast off his grey-headed servants when no longer capable of labouring as they have done. The Lord often strengthens his people in their souls, when nature is sinking into decay. And it is a debt which the old disciples of Christ owe to succeeding generations, to leave behind them a solemn testimony to the advantage of religion, and the truth of God's promises; and especially to the everlasting righteousness of the Redeemer. Assured of deliverance and victory, let us spend our days, while waiting the approach of death, in praising the Holy One of Israel with all our powers. And while speaking of his righteousness, and singing his praises, we shall rise above fears and infirmities, and have earnests of the joys of heaven. The work of redemption ought, above all God's works, to be spoken of by us in our praises. The Lamb that was slain, and has redeemed us to God, is worthy of all blessing and praise.
